source: Claude draft, 2026-10-13. Not yet checked by a native speaker.

entries.qa: Gender: masculine speaker form (matches 'Enchanté' in the vetted file); a woman writes 'Désolée', same pronunciation. For bumping into someone or getting past, 'Pardon.' is the usual word.

entries.target: Une table pour ___, s'il vous plaît.
entries.pronunciation_easy: ewn TAH-bluh poor, seel voo PLEH
entries.qa: Blank takes a bare number (deux, trois...). For one person say 'pour une personne' rather than 'pour un'. 'pour deux personnes' is equally natural.
'La carte' is the menu list. 'Le menu' in France usually means a fixed-price set menu, so 'la carte' is the safer word.

SAFETY. Back-translation: 'I am allergic [to the] ___.' The blank must include à + article, which contracts and changes per word (au gluten, au lait, aux œufs, aux fruits à coque, à la ..., à l'...), so 'à' is not outside the blank. 'allergique' is the same for male and female speakers.
Gender: masculine speaker form; a woman says 'Je suis végétarienne' (vay-zhay-tah-RYEN, with the final n pronounced, not nasal).

SAFETY. Back-translation: 'Without ___, please.' No article after 'sans' (sans viande, sans lait, sans gluten). This is a preference request; for a real allergy use allergic_to as well, since 'sans' alone may be read as taste, not medical need.
Gender of the thing, not the speaker: 'Un autre' for a masculine item (un café, un verre), 'Une autre' (ew-NOH-truh) for a feminine one (une bière).

entries.target: Un billet pour ___, s'il vous plaît.
entries.pronunciation_easy: uhn bee-YEH poor, seel voo PLEH
entries.qa: Usually filled with a city name (pour Lyon). 'pour' does not contract, so the word's own article stays (pour la gare, pour le centre-ville).

Blank takes à + article, which contracts per word (à l'aéroport, au centre-ville, à la gare), so 'à' stays inside the blank. 'il' = the bus/train/metro/tram, all masculine. Reviewer: 'Ce bus va à ___ ?' is an alternative if the vehicle is named.

Blank takes à + article, contracting per word (à l'aéroport, au centre-ville). In a taxi people very often just say the destination: 'À l'aéroport, s'il vous plaît.' A softer option is 'Vous pouvez m'emmener ___ ?'
Reviewer: 'Vous pouvez vous arrêter ici ?' or simply 'Ici, s'il vous plaît.' are also common to a taxi driver.

entries.target: Le prochain part à quelle heure ?
entries.pronunciation_easy: luh proh-SHAN par ah kel UHR
entries.qa: 'Le prochain' assumes a masculine vehicle (train, bus). For a feminine one (une navette) it is 'La prochaine'.
'quai' = platform, understood everywhere. French train departure boards show 'Voie' (track), so travellers may also hear/ask 'C'est quelle voie ?'
Gender: masculine speaker form; a woman writes 'Je suis perdue', same pronunciation.

entries.target: Vous pouvez me montrer sur la carte ?
entries.pronunciation_easy: voo poo-VAY muh mohn-TRAY sewr lah KART

entries.qa: 'de' becomes d' before a name starting with a vowel or mute h (Au nom d'Anderson).

entries.target: Quel est le mot de passe du wifi ?
entries.pronunciation_easy: kel eh luh moh duh PAHSS dew wee-FEE

entries.target: À quelle heure faut-il libérer la chambre ?
entries.pronunciation_easy: ah kel uhr foh-TEEL lee-bay-RAY lah SHAHN-bruh
entries.qa: Reviewer: natural hotel phrasing is 'libérer la chambre' (vacate the room). 'Le check-out est à quelle heure ?' is also widely used in hotels.

entries.target: Je peux laisser mes bagages ici ?
entries.pronunciation_easy: zhuh puh leh-SAY may bah-GAHZH ee-SEE

entries.qa: Blank takes the noun with its article (La douche ne marche pas). 'ne fonctionne pas' is a slightly more formal synonym. For hot water, 'Il n'y a pas d'eau chaude' (there's no hot water) is more idiomatic than the filled frame.

entries.target: Je peux avoir une autre serviette ?
entries.qa: 'serviette' is also a table napkin; in a hotel room it is understood as towel. 'serviette de bain' if it needs to be explicit.
Gender of the item, not the speaker: 'le' for a masculine item, 'la' for a feminine one (Je la prends), 'les' for plural.

entries.target: Vous l'avez dans une autre taille ?
entries.qa: For shoes the word is 'pointure' (dans une autre pointure).

Reviewer: 'rafraîchir' (refresh) is the usual salon/barber word for a trim; 'juste égaliser' (just even it out) or 'juste les pointes' (just the ends) are alternatives. Not fully sure which is most natural at a men's barber.

entries.target: Une taille de barbe, s'il vous plaît.
entries.pronunciation_easy: ewn TIE duh BARB, seel voo PLEH
entries.qa: 'Taille de barbe' is the usual barber-menu term. Reviewer: 'Vous pouvez me tailler la barbe ?' is a verb alternative.
SAFETY. Back-translation: 'Help!' (literally 'to the rescue'). The standard French cry for help.
SAFETY. Back-translation: 'Call the police!' (polite/plural vous imperative, right for strangers). Emergency number in France: 17 or 112.
SAFETY. Back-translation: 'I have need of a doctor.' = I need a doctor. Same for male and female speakers.
SAFETY. Back-translation: 'Where is the pharmacy?' For any pharmacy nearby, 'Il y a une pharmacie près d'ici ?' (Is there a pharmacy near here?) also works.
SAFETY. Back-translation: 'It is an emergency.' Standard phrasing.

SAFETY. Back-translation: 'I have lost ___.' The blank takes a possessive that changes with the noun (mon passeport, ma valise, mes clés), so it stays inside the blank. 'perdu' does not change for speaker gender here.

entries.target: Je ne me sens pas bien.
entries.pronunciation_easy: zhuh nuh muh sahn pah BYEN
entries.qa: SAFETY. Back-translation: 'I don't feel myself well.' = I don't feel well. Same for male and female speakers.
SAFETY. Back-translation: 'I must call someone.' 'J'ai besoin d'appeler quelqu'un' (I need to call someone) is an equally natural alternative.

anything_else.qa: Shop staff very often say 'Et avec ceci ?' (ay ah-vek suh-SEE), 'And with this?', meaning the same.

here_you_go.qa: 'Tenez.' (tuh-NAY) is also common when handing something over.

inside_or_outside.qa: Waiters also say 'En salle ou en terrasse ?'

receipt_question.qa: In shops and cafés the receipt is usually 'le ticket'; 'un reçu' is also heard.

how_would_you_like_it.qa: Uncertain: also 'Qu'est-ce qu'on vous fait ?' (What are we doing for you?). Phrasing varies by barber.
